claims.text: The proposed FeCoNi-based alloy is fcc.
The proposed alloy contains a minor addition of Al.
The proposed composition has configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
Minor Al incorporation preserves the high saturation magnetization of the FeCoNi-based alloy.
Homogenization near 1000 °C followed by cooling with a hold near 600 °C for several hours will induce incipient chemical ordering.
The thermal treatment will generate nanoscale L1_2-type ordered domains.
The ordered domains will remain embedded in a predominantly disordered fcc matrix.
Partial L1_2-type ordering will create coherent antiphase boundaries.
The ordered regions will have higher magnetic anisotropy than the disordered matrix.
Antiphase boundaries between ordered and disordered regions will pin magnetic domain walls.
Domain-wall pinning by the antiphase boundaries will increase coercivity.
Controlled partial ordering will retain high saturation magnetization.
The treated alloy will have significantly greater coercivity than a fully disordered FeCoNi-based baseline.
Excessive ordering could destabilize the high-entropy phase or substantially reduce saturation magnetization.

contradictions.description: The initial-state and boundary fields specify only a minor Al addition while calling the alloy nearly equiatomic, whereas the experiment specifies equiatomic FeCoNiAl, conventionally implying 25 at.% Al. A minor fourth-element addition and an equiatomic quaternary composition are not the same composition.

The hypothesis implies comparison with a fully disordered counterpart of the same Al-containing composition, but the stated baseline can be read as Al-free equiatomic FeCoNi, while the experimental control is FeCoNiAl. The baseline composition is therefore inconsistent or insufficiently defined.
